subject: EdgeCommerce renewal: converting burst to committed capacity + rate tiers
messages:
From: Eliza Park <eliza.park@edgecommerce.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-18T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning + question about converting burst to committed capacity

Hi Karthik,

Hope you’re well. We’re starting renewal planning for our hosted API usage (EdgeCommerce). Q3 was higher than forecasted — we used a lot of burst credits around peak shopping windows. Instead of relying on burst again, the execs want predictable unit economics and lower per-token rates. Can you outline what converting our seasonal burst volume into a committed monthly commit looks like (pricing, invoice cadence, any minimum term changes)? Also flagged procurement: procurement@edgecommerce.com.

I attached the Q3 usage summary to this message. Next week would work for a quick sync.

Thanks,
Eliza
Head of Platforms
EdgeCommerce

Attachment: EdgeCommerce_Q3_usage_summary.csv (summary only, 2MB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Park <eliza.park@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-18T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + question about converting burst to committed capacity

Eliza — thanks for the note and the usage file. Quick read shows two clear paths:

1) Short-term: add a mid-year committed top-up aligned to your peak months (3–6 months) and keep a smaller burst buffer. Faster to approve, lower legal friction.
2) Annualize: convert a portion of the burst used in Q3 into a higher monthly commit with a 12-month term in exchange for a revised per-token rate. This gives predictability and material unit-cost savings.

I’ve looped in Marissa (renewals) and Naomi (billing/pricing) to sketch numbers and the mutual action plan (MOP). Can we schedule a 30-min on Tue 10/19 or Wed 10/20? I’ll bring a concrete proposal and a sample MOP.

—Karthik
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Park <eliza.park@edgecommerce.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal planning + question about converting burst to committed capacity

Eliza — appreciated the call earlier. Recap and next steps from Redwood:  

- Proposal: Convert 60% of the observed Q3 burst consumption into a monthly committed baseline (12-month term).  
- Pricing: commit band discount applied at the new monthly commit level; estimated blended rate reduction ~18% on generation tokens vs current burst-adjusted pricing. Exact numbers below once we confirm the commit quantity.
- Operational changes: add a soft throttle guard and a 10% monthly burst pocket for unexpected spikes (no extra cost for first two months to ease transition).
- Invoicing: prefer monthly invoicing aligned with commit; we can support quarterly invoicing if procurement needs consolidated POs.

Action items for EdgeCommerce: share the contract approver and preferred invoicing cadence; procurement@edgecommerce.com will be okay input. We’ll attach a draft MOP and a simple one-line amendment template to make legal review quicker.

Attachments: Draft_MOP_EdgeCommerce_v1.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Renewals
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing sketch for EdgeCommerce

Quick pricing sketch (internal):

- Current baseline avg token cost (Q3 effective): $0.00120/token (generation)
- If we convert 60% of burst => monthly commit = ~180B tokens/mo => proposed tiered pricing: first 100B @ $0.00098, next 60B @ $0.00085, overflow @ standard hosted rate.
- Estimated monthly invoice impact vs today: +25% spend predictable vs large variance, with ~18% unit price improvement.
- Upsell credit: offer a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent of 10% of first month commit) to offset contract switch costs.

Naomi — can you confirm whether quarterly invoicing impacts recognition or if we need an AR hold for a PO > $250k?

—Priyom
Account Strategy

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Eliza Park <eliza.park@edgecommerce.com>, procurement@edgecommerce.com
Date: 2027-10-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal invoicing options and PO parameters

Thanks team — procurement note for EdgeCommerce:

- We can support monthly or quarterly invoicing. If EdgeCommerce prefers quarterly POs, we’ll need a single master PO referencing the amendment and the yearly commit schedule.
- For PO > $250k we do an AR verification step; timeline for verification is typically 3–5 business days after PO submission.
- Legal redline: amendment will be a short addendum that updates committed token quantities, rates, and burst pocket. No SLA changes.

Eliza / Sam: if you can confirm preferred cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and the PO owner, we’ll put the MOP into the doc for signatures and prepare a DocuSign link.

Naomi
Senior Finance Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Riley <sam.riley@edgecommerce.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Eliza Park <eliza.park@edgecommerce.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@edgecommerce.com
Date: 2027-10-21T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal invoicing options and PO parameters

Naomi — procurement prefers quarterly POs (internal cadence). PO owner will be procurement@edgecommerce.com. We’ll aim to get the first quarter PO to you by 11/05. A few questions from procurement:

1) Can the amendment show the monthly commit schedule and the quarterly invoicing mapping?
2) How will overage be billed if we exceed the committed baseline in a given month?

We’re happy to proceed with the 12-month commit as long as the invoicing syncs with our internal finance windows.

Thanks,
Sam
VP Ops, EdgeCommerce

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Park <eliza.park@edgecommerce.com>, Sam Riley <sam.riley@edgecommerce.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-25T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeCommerce renewal: converting burst to committed capacity + rate tiers (final MOP & next steps)

Thanks everyone — agreed path and next steps below:  

- Commit structure: convert 60% of Q3 burst into a 12-mo monthly commit (start 11/01). Priyom and Marissa to finalize exact commit number and rates; internal sketch shared earlier.
- Invoice cadence: quarterly POs ok — Naomi will prepare the amendment showing monthly commit schedule + quarterly invoicing mapping.
- Overage handling: overflow billed at the agreed overflow rate (same banding as proposal); we’ll include an automatic alert at 85% usage with a one-click temporary burst top-up option.
- Timeline: Redwood to send DocuSign amendment + MOP by 10/28. EdgeCommerce procurement to return PO by 11/05. AR verification window 3–5 business days on receipt.

I’ve attached the Draft_MOP_EdgeCommerce_v1.pdf for internal review and the usage CSV Eliza sent. If that timeline works I’ll lock the DocuSign and cc procurement.

Next steps (owners):
- Marissa: finalize rates & populate DocuSign (due 10/28)
- Naomi: build invoice mapping + AR note (due 10/28)
- Sam/Eliza: procurement PO by 11/05
- Priyom: confirm onboarding credit calculation

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the DocuSign link once live.

—Karthik
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
